newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Debts, bureacracy delay Bulgaria's privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Debts, bureacracy delay Bulgaria's privatisation.

text.p: Privatisations to raise badly needed cash are being delayed by bad debts of the enterprises offered for sale, slow concession procedures and bureacracy, the head of Bulgaria's privatisation agency said on Friday.
The government has announced that it will offer for sale 18 major state enterprises by early 1997 to raise funds to meet debt payments.
"There are serious concession problems with five of the 18 enterprises earmarked for sale in the next months," executive director Vesselin Blagoev told a news conference.
These include the copper smelter in Pirdop, and the ship repair docks at the Black Sea port of Bourgas.
Bulgaria passed a concession law earlier this year but not a single concession has been granted, said Blagoev.
"The balance sheets of some of these enterprises are burdened with bad debts which would delay their legal analysis," said Blagoev.
On Thursday, the government approved the sale of a 60 percent stake in its Sodi Devnya chemical complex to U.S. firm General Chemical Group Inc for $160 million.
"We will begin preparing the contracts next week and hope to close the deal in the next 10 days," said Blagoev.
The deal does not include a concession on the nearby limestone and salt deposits, which are the basic inputs for the standard soda ash produced by Sodi Devnya.
The buyer is expected to sign a supply contract with the government.

The deal has yet to be approved by the agency's supervisory baord which resigned earlier this year over disagreements with the Socialist government. A new board had not been set up by the November 11 deadline.
